purpose: Give SEIS a safe way to recognize, classify, plan, and route every GitHub-known language without pretending every language is an active runtime dependency.

officialSource.name: GitHub Linguist languages.yml
officialSource.sourceDescription: Defines all languages known to GitHub with type, ace_mode, extensions, filenames, language_id, tm_scope, aliases, color, group, interpreters, and wrapping metadata.

corePolicy: SEIS may recognize every GitHub-known language as catalog metadata.
SEIS must not activate every language as a runtime, dependency, compiler, interpreter, SDK, or build tool.
Language recognition is safe; language execution is approval-gated.
Every language must be routed to a purpose, family, risk tier, and validation lane before implementation.
Current working SEIS web surfaces remain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript first until a scoped PR proves a new runtime is needed.

activationTiers.label: Active SEIS Core
activationTiers.meaning: Already part of the current local-first SEIS repository workflow.

activationTiers.label: Ready Extension
activationTiers.meaning: Can be added when a product surface needs it and validation exists.

activationTiers.label: Contract Only
activationTiers.meaning: May appear in docs, examples, parsers, schemas, or compatibility notes but not as live runtime yet.

activationTiers.label: Reference Only
activationTiers.meaning: Recognized for search, indexing, file classification, import/export, docs, and education.

activationTiers.label: Blocked Until Approval
activationTiers.meaning: Requires new SDKs, compilers, interpreters, emulators, VM runtimes, GPU stacks, cloud services, or security review.
activationTiers.approval: explicit human approval plus isolated branch

languageFamilies.label: Web, Markup, and Product Surfaces
languageFamilies.seisUse: Website, Desktop OS, docs, product UI, local demo pages, content rendering.

languageFamilies.label: Systems and Native
languageFamilies.seisUse: Future system lab, native apps, Apple-first work, low-level tooling research.

languageFamilies.label: Backend and Enterprise
languageFamilies.seisUse: APIs, provider routers, enterprise service lanes, integrations, future durable backend.

languageFamilies.label: Data, AI, and Science
languageFamilies.seisUse: RAG, evaluation, analytics, datasets, typed contracts, AI governance, data import/export.

languageFamilies.label: DevOps, Config, and Infrastructure
languageFamilies.seisUse: CI, local checks, cloud readiness, server configs, deployment plans, SSH-safe onboarding.

languageFamilies.label: Formal Methods and Research
languageFamilies.seisUse: Future verification, proof-oriented docs, specification research, agent correctness experiments.

languageFamilies.label: Creative, Media, Audio, and Graphics
languageFamilies.seisUse: Creative coding, audio/visual experiments, 3D assets, motion systems, design tech research.

languageFamilies.label: Legacy, Specialized, and Esoteric
languageFamilies.seisUse: Recognition, docs, compatibility catalog, search/indexing, educational reference only.

safeImplementationModes.label: Recognize
safeImplementationModes.meaning: SEIS can identify and display the language in search, files, docs, and catalogs.

safeImplementationModes.label: Document
safeImplementationModes.meaning: SEIS can explain where the language would fit and why.

safeImplementationModes.label: Parse Metadata
safeImplementationModes.meaning: SEIS can ingest file extension, color, aliases, and language family metadata.

safeImplementationModes.label: Validate Contract
safeImplementationModes.meaning: SEIS can validate JSON/docs/schema references before executing anything.

safeImplementationModes.label: Execute Runtime
safeImplementationModes.meaning: Blocked until explicit approval, dependency plan, sandbox boundary, and rollback exist.

blockedWithoutApproval: installing compilers, interpreters, package managers, SDKs, engines, emulators, or GPU toolkits
executing untrusted code in any recognized language
adding build systems for every recognized language
turning reference-only languages into production dependencies
running Docker, Kubernetes, cloud, SSH, provider, database, or deployment actions
claiming SEIS supports every language at runtime before validators and isolated sandboxes exist
